subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw treat enrolled-speaker matching as a supported gate for voice-triggered actions, and if so which native/realtime paths, storage model, provider egress rules, and fallback policy should be in scope first?
rationale: The request is valid but crosses biometric-like local state, probabilistic authorization, provider audio egress, config/settings surfaces, and native app/runtime ownership that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design speaker gate contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved contract for enrollment, matching confidence, fallback, storage/deletion, provider use, and initial platform scope before code.

options.title: Narrow to provider diarization only
options.body: Limit the first implementation to provider-returned speaker labels for transcription cleanup, without treating speaker identity as an authorization or wake-action gate.

options.title: Defer enrolled voice gating
options.body: Keep current wake-word/PTT/Talk behavior and revisit speaker recognition only after native voice and provider extension points mature further.

recommendation.title: Design speaker gate contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved contract for enrollment, matching confidence, fallback, storage/deletion, provider use, and initial platform scope before code.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history across native voice runtime, Android Talk/PTT fixes, realtime voice provider behavior, and maintainer-side merge routing for this surface.
